title: prompt-library-scratchpad-jordan-kim-experiments
content:
Purpose: quick personal scratchpad for prompt templates + few-shot sets + observed failure modes. Iterate before pushing to prompt-library repo. Mostly rough notes and examples; not polished.

Goals:
- Build compact, reusable prompt templates for chat-completion and instruction-following tasks.
- Collect few-shot exemplars that generalize across similar user intents.
- Surface failure cases and mitigation strategies (temperature, system prompt, post-filtering).

High-level constraints: keep prompts <= 2400 tokens when combined with few-shot samples for target toy test cases. Prefer explicit output formats (JSON or bullet lists) to reduce hallucination.

1) Generic instruction-following template (single-turn)
Template: 
System: You are a helpful, concise assistant that returns only the data requested in valid JSON. If the user asks for steps, return an array of strings under key "steps".
User: {{instruction}}

Notes: use when we need structured outputs. Add "max_tokens" budget ~ 200 for short instructions.

2) Summarization template (long-doc -> short)
Template: 
System: Summarize the following document into a 2-3 sentence executive summary plus 3 key bullets. Output as JSON with keys: "summary", "bullets". Do not add information not present in the document.
User: Document: {{document_text}}

Few-shot examples (for summarization):
Example 1 input (doc): The company shipped v1.2 with bug fixes for memory leak in worker pool. Customers reported 10% faster response time on average after fix.
Example 1 output (JSON): {"summary": "Release v1.2 fixed a worker pool memory leak and improved response latency.", "bullets": ["Fixed memory leak in worker pool", "~10% average response improvement", "Backfilled tests and rollback plan available"]}

Example 2 input (doc): Research notes: we benchmarked quantized LLM on A100 showing 2.4x cost reduction at 1.5% token-level perplexity increase.
Example 2 output (JSON): {"summary": "Quantized model benchmarks show substantial cost savings with small quality degradation.", "bullets": ["2.4x cost reduction", "~1.5% token-level perplexity increase", "Suitable for high-throughput non-critical tasks"]}

Failure modes observed (summarization):
- Model hallucinates facts when the document is very short or uses ambiguous pronouns. Mitigation: increase context window (include surrounding sentences) or bias toward "cannot determine" when confidence low.
- Numeric distortion: percentages rounded inconsistently. Mitigation: ask model to preserve numeric tokens as-is or output "as-stated" field.

3) Intent classification (compact few-shot)
Template: 
System: Classify the user message into one of: [question, command, feedback, bug_report, billing_query]. Return a single token label.
User: "{{user_message}}"

Few-shot set:
- "How do I add an API key?" -> question
- "Rotate customer A keys and revoke old tokens." -> command
- "The embedding quality dropped after the patch." -> bug_report
- "I want a pricing estimate for dedicated capacity." -> billing_query
- "Your new UI is great!" -> feedback

Edge cases & notes:
- Short messages like "thanks" sometimes misclassify as feedback or question; add punctuation or use a threshold where "thanks" maps to feedback default.
- Messages containing both question + command: heuristics prefer "command" for operational instructions.

4) Few-shot generator for slot-filling (entities)
Target: extract {customer, environment, model, region, priority} from support texts.
Template:
System: Extract entities and return JSON with keys: "customer", "environment", "model", "region", "priority". If missing, return null.
User: "{{text}}"

Few-shot exemplars:
- "Customer Acme corp seeing errors on staging when calling /v1/generate with ada-003 in us-west1, urgent" -> {"customer": "Acme Corp", "environment": "staging", "model": "ada-003", "region": "us-west1", "priority": "urgent"}
- "We noticed increased latency in prod for call to /v1/embeddings using text-embedding-3-large" -> "priority": null, "environment": "prod" etc.

Failure cases (slot-filling):
- Model invents company names when shorthand used ("ACME" -> writes "Acme Incorporated"). Normalize by asking for exact string or return original substring.
- Misses region tags when user writes "westus" vs "us-west1". Add normalization mapping post-process.

5) Testing harness notes (quick):
- Local eval: run curl against hosted playground to confirm JSON-only output. Use low temperature (0.0-0.2) for deterministic outputs.
- A/B: compare 10 random samples with temperature 0.0 vs 0.3; measure label stability and token variance.
- Eval metrics to track: structure-validity %, exact-match on keys, numeric-preservation rate.

6) Prompt mutation experiments (ideas to try):
- Add explicit "If you are unsure, output: {\"uncertain\": true}" clause.
- Use chain-of-thought style only in internal tests (not for production) to see if it improves extraction.
- Try progressive disclosure: start with concise system prompt; if output invalid, re-run with stronger constraints.

7) Quick checklist before committing to prompt-library repo:
- [ ] Convert template variables to clear markers ({{}}) and document expected types.
- [ ] Add 5–10 diverse few-shot exemplars per intent.
- [ ] Add automated tests (schema validation + 50 sample inputs).
- [ ] Note expected failure modes and mitigation steps in README.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Which set of exemplar diversity do we standardize on for classification? (Samira: recommended stratified sampling across short/long/ambiguous).
- Decide canonical JSON schema for summarization outputs (include "source_excerpt"?).
- Add a small section about rate-limiting experiments (how heavy few-shot impacts latency).

Notes-to-self: commit partial examples to branch prompt-library/compact-templates, ping Lee for quick review.

Recent quick tests (local):
- Summarization template with 2 examples + doc of 300 tokens -> structure-valid 92%, hallucination flagged in 8%.
- Intent classifier (5-shot) on 200 messages -> accuracy ~88% (drops on terse Slack-like messages).

End of scratchpad. Will tidy and push in next pass.
